A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lentiviral system is a viable candidate for gene therapy of lysosomal storage disorders, and in particular for GM2 ganglioidosis.
lentiviral vector mediated gene therapy is effective in the CNS following systemic administration in neonatal mice.
the FIV(HEx) lentiviral vector can be successfully transferred to the brain of Hexb-deficient mice after intraperitoneal injection and ameliorates disease progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FIV(HEXB) may represent a new tool for the treatment of lysosomal storage disorders, including Sandhoff disease, and other neurodegenerative disorders.
lentiviral vectors are a promising approach to treat CNS diseases, and that systemic administration to neonates may provide a viable strategy to treat lysosomal storage diseases.
